hypothesis: Iter 80 = TWO structural mechanisms, both attributable against the honest iter-79 baseline (gate FAILED there: glucose_mape 0.2018 > 0.20 knife-edge, verifier_cat[meal] 0.588 < 0.65, skill_vs_persistence(real) negative on every marker incl. glucose -20.1). Local diagnosis of the landed iter-79 model (gs://grovina-pulse-data/training/jobs/iter79/model.pt) found the meal/glucose failure is STRUCTURAL, not a supervision gap: dose-response already ran peak-mode at weight 0.40 (glucose:peak:0.7:0.25, target 0.7 mg/dL/g) yet the model realised only ~0.16 mg/dL/g (a 60 g meal raised glucose ~14 mg/dL, not ~30-50). Glucose was the one metabolic species still on a plain SpeciesHead, so meal->glucose amplitude had to be discovered by an MLP that simultaneously holds the fasting equilibrium — the softplus-saturation trap GlucoseGatedInsulinHead / BasalPlusGatedPeakHead were built to escape for insulin/glucagon/FFA. MECHANISM 1 (learned model, MetabolicModule.log_ra): structural glucose rate-of-appearance term dG += Ra·gut_glucose_appearance, mirroring the minimal-model Ra(t) source (Dalla Man 2007) the teacher carries explicitly and the symmetric complement of the existing structural clearance term log_sg. coupling[0] (gut glucose-appearance) is >=0 and ~0 between meals, so the term is SILENT fasted (gate-safe) and fires only postprandially — exactly the axis dose-response supervises. Init Ra=0.55 calibrated locally so 60 g lands ~0.5 mg/dL/g (sensitivity 0.41) at the iter-79 operating point: in-band at cold start, below the 0.7 target so dose-response ramps UP (no overshoot of the knife-edge gate). Gradient verified to reach log_ra through a meal rollout — the amplitude is now a single scalar the existing dose-response gradient moves directly, instead of a buried-MLP parameter no strong gradient reached. MECHANISM 2 (teacher, full_body): hepatic-output split + glycogen->ketosis coupling. The lumped Hep is partitioned into a glycogenolytic share (scaled by liver-glycogen availability glyco_avail = (LGly/(LGly+K_L)) / (LGly_b/(LGly_b+K_L))) and a gluconeogenic share with partial compensation. CONSERVATION-EXACT at the fed calibration state (glyco_avail=1 => identity): verified acute OGTT byte-identical to the pre-iter-80 teacher (max|Δglucose/insulin/bhb| < 0.005), and a fed day max|Δglucose|=0.015 mg/dL — so the acute gate sees NO change. The split diverges only as the liver depletes (>12 h fast). Because blood glucose is homeostatically defended, the glucose-side divergence alone is sub-noise (~0.3 mg/dL at 35 h) — so the load-bearing coupling is glycogen->KETOSIS: ketogenesis ramps with (1 - glyco_avail), lifting 24 h fasting BHB from the teacher's too-flat ~0.25 mM to ~1.24 mM (Cahill 2006 range), and 36 h to ~2.1 mM. BHB actually MOVES in fasting, so this is what finally gives the slow glycogen pool a strong, observable gradient (distilled via cold-distill markers bhb/liver_glycogen/muscle_glycogen on the fast_24h protocol) — the supervision iters 55-57 lacked. The two mechanisms are orthogonal (Mech 1 = acute postprandial glucose amplitude; Mech 2 = >12 h fasting fuel switch, conservation-exact acutely) so a regression on either is attributable. WHY ALL-IN (not split across iters): a conservation-exact teacher split cannot confound the acute glucose metric by construction, so the iter-69 'bundling kills attribution' scar does not apply here; and Mech 1 buys the glucose headroom the prep-review flagged the slow-pool feedback needs on the knife-edge. CONFIG HELD BYTE-IDENTICAL to iter 79 (all 48 trainArgs unchanged): both mechanisms are STRUCTURAL — Mech 1 is trained by the existing dose-response signal, Mech 2 flows into the existing cold-distill / cohort / trajectory targets — so the benchmark is attributable to exactly these two architecture/teacher changes, nothing else.

SECONDARY (north star): (5) liver_glycogen / muscle_glycogen pools get their first STRONG gradient via the glycogen->ketosis edge — watch dist_liver_glycogen / dist_bhb in cold-distill telemetry on the fast_24h protocol; if BHB now tracks the teacher's ~1.2 mM fasting rise, the slow pool has a stable closed-loop base for future chronic-block work. LOCAL GATE before/after dispatch: scripts/iter80_gate.py asserts gut->glucose sensitivity in 0.40-0.90 mg/dL/g, acute OGTT conservation < 0.05, and 24 h fasting BHB in 0.8-3.0 mM — all PASS on the candidate architecture.
